extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in international/postwar affairs
extracted.subtask_description: A multipiece Associated Press-style news article reporting diplomatic, military, legal and political developments in East Asia and the Pacific in the immediate post‑World War II period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guarantee of China's independence
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan provided for Japan and America to guarantee the independence of China.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Konoye wrote that the American-Japanese compromise plan would have both nations guarantee China's independence as a central term of settlement of the China hostilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Japanese withdrawal from Chinese territory
rubrics_metrics.description: Japan was to withdraw her troops from Chinese territory 'based on an agreement to be formed between Japanese and Chinese.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This was presented as a condition tied to a negotiated settlement with Chinese authorities rather than unilateral evacuation; it is part of the proposed framework to settle the China question.

rubrics_metrics.name: No annexation and no reparations
rubrics_metrics.description: There would be no annexation of Chinese territory, no reparations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These were explicit terms of the American-Japanese trial plans described in Konoye's memoirs as a way to reassure China and facilitate rapprochement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival of the Open Door policy / union of Chinese regimes
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan called for revival of the open door policy and 'union of the Chiang and Wang regimes' (i.e., rapprochement between Chungking and the Japanese-sponsored puppet government).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The revival of the open door and political reconciliation between rival Chinese authorities were listed as components of the settlement aimed at restoring stability and trade access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-restriction on Japanese immigration into Chinese territory
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-restriction by Japan of immigration of Japanese into Chinese territory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of the compromise plan Japan would limit immigration into China to reduce tensions and demographic pressure cited in the memoirs.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. recognition of Manchoukuo (as proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: American recognition of Manchoukuo, the state which Japan had established in Manchuria, was listed as a proposed element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Konoye's account includes this controversial concession as part of the package discussed in 1941 negotiations; presented as an item in the plan rather than an uncontested fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑positioning of naval and air forces so as to mutually threaten
rubrics_metrics.description: America and Japan 'will not position naval and air strength which would mutually threaten the other' in the Japanese-American negotiations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This term aimed to limit mutual force deployments in the Pacific to reduce tensions and was framed as part of military/security confidence-building measures in the plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual exchange and supply of necessary materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision for mutual exchange of necessary materials and American credit/support to supply Japan with resources (petroleum, rubber, tin, nickel, etc.) Japan desired in the southwest Pacific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan contemplated economic cooperation and material exchanges to satisfy Japan's resource needs and to underpin a political settlement fostering peaceful relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint guarantee of Philippine independence
rubrics_metrics.description: The two countries would jointly guarantee the independence of the Philippines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in the plan as a regional security confidence measure: joint guarantees to third countries as part of broader reconciliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treaty clause guaranteeing a reciprocal free press and open communications facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: General MacArthur recommended inclusion in all United States treaties of a clause guaranteeing 'a reciprocal free press and open communications facilities.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MacArthur argued such a clause would provide a greater guarantee of an international free press and serve as an example for other nations; he contrasted free press with use of the press for propaganda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free press must not be used as propaganda
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the press is turned to propaganda its value is lost and with it the foundation for the evil (isms); nothing will destroy a free press more quickly than a propaganda press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MacArthur's commentary frames a normative standard for press behavior and for treaty provisions: support unfettered, non‑propagandistic operation of the press as essential to democracy and international example-setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atomic energy governance may require international (world) political solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: The solutions of the problems presented by atomic energy must be sought in the realm of world politics; some form of world government may be necessary to maintain peace in the atomic age, with a limited surrender of national sovereignty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expressed by Prime Minister Mackenzie King (Canada) as a policy/standard for international organization and restraint in the atomic era, implying institutional/sovereign tradeoffs to control proliferation and manage resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for challenging a military commission's jurisdiction (Yamashita case)
rubrics_metrics.description: Argument that when the commission was appointed there was no military government or hostilities in the Philippine Islands and therefore no authority to set it up; petitioners contend the military commission was illegal and civil courts should have jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as the legal basis for Supreme Court review and for granting stays of execution pending determination of whether military tribunals had proper authority; the news notes stays in death cases pending review are usual practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay of execution pending higher court review in capital/military cases
rubrics_metrics.description: It was believed unprecedented for a foreign enemy general to appeal to the Supreme Court, but it is usual for the court in a death case to grant a stay pending decision on whether the appeal should be reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting of Supreme Court practice: stays of execution are often granted to permit consideration of whether extraordinary relief (review) should be taken in capital cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules of RAF/British aerial operations in Java
rubrics_metrics.description: British planes are used only to protect displaced persons when troops cannot control the situation, or when there is hostile action against British troops; Dutch armed planes are not permitted in Java.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issued as a statement of operational policy and rules of engagement for Allied air operations in the Netherlands East Indies area; explains limited mission scope and reasons for restrictions on Dutch aircraft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational airlift capacity and airfield handling preparations for Manchuria
rubrics_metrics.description: Airlift preparations reported: C-54 transport planes each capable of fifty or more fully equipped infantrymen were scheduled to begin operations; advance preparations made for handling the huge planes on Mukden and Harbin air fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article cites logistical capacity (plane type and troop capacity) and required airfield handling/preparations as operational prerequisites for planned troop movements into Manchuria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extraterritorial rights protest standard
rubrics_metrics.description: France has not yet formally relinquished extraterritorial rights in China; the French consulate protested vigorously against the arrest by Chinese of a French national, calling it a flouting of extraterritorial rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reflects the diplomatic/legal standard that until formally relinquished, extraterritorial privileges remain in force and arrests of foreign nationals by local authorities can be protested as violations of those rights.
